en: Contrary to popular belief, Emilio Aguinaldo, not Jose Rizal, served as the first president of the Philippine Republic in 1899.
Many mistakenly call the Waling-waling the national flower, but the Sampaguita officially holds that title, declared in 1934.
Although the President leads the country, only the Legislative branch, composed of the Senate and House of Representatives, can create laws.
Many think the flag's white triangle represents peace, but it actually symbolizes the Katipunan, the secret society that started the revolution.
People often think Igorot is a single tribe, but it is actually an umbrella term for several distinct ethnolinguistic groups in the Cordilleras.
While often confused, Filipino is the national language that incorporates words from various Philippine languages, whereas Tagalog is just one specific regional language.
Many assume Sinulog honors a national hero, but this Cebu festival actually celebrates the Santo Niño, the child Jesus, through street dancing.
Contrary to the belief that everyone pays income tax, minimum wage earners in the Philippines are actually exempt from paying personal income tax.
People often confuse utang na loob with financial debt, but it actually refers to a deep, non-material sense of gratitude and reciprocal loyalty.
Many think the videophone was an American invention, but Filipino scientist Gregorio Zara actually invented the first two-way videophone in 1955.
Although July 4, 1946, marks US recognition, the Philippines officially celebrates its true Independence Day on June 12, commemorating the 1898 proclamation.
Many mistakenly believe Spoliarium shows a chariot race, but the painting actually depicts dead gladiators being dragged away in an ancient Roman arena.
